docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Unit tests for NetworkIO — the component responsible for managing all socket connections, handling the epoll event loop, sending outbound packets, and delivering inbound packets to the parser queue as RxPacket structs.

Tests are written with Google Test (gtest). The test suite spins up fake TCP servers and UDP senders on localhost to exercise the full network I/O path without requiring real exchange connectivity.

docs.title: Test Environment
docs.text:
Component Role FakeTCPServer Accepts connections, receives sent data, sends test packets back — one instance per TCP session FakeUDPSender Sends UDP datagrams to NetworkIO's bound ports NetworkIO System under test — runs recv_send() on a dedicated thread Builder_Dispatch Used to generate outbound TxPackets from test orders SessionManager Tracks login state per session

Five sessions are simulated:

Session Port Transport Venue Protocol 0 9876 TCP BIST FIX 1 1234 TCP BIST OUCH 2 4321 TCP NASDAQ OUCH 3 5000 UDP BIST ITCH 4 6000 UDP NASDAQ ITCH

docs.title: NetworkIOTest.NetworkIOTestAll
docs.text: End-to-end integration of the full NetworkIO path — connection establishment, session login, outbound order sending, and inbound packet delivery across all five sessions simultaneously.

docs.title: 1. Socket Initialization
docs.text:
Verifies that NetworkIO correctly initializes socket state for each TCP session before the event loop starts.

Checked fields:

  • connection_pending is true for all three TCP sessions — sockets have called ::connect() and are waiting for the handshake (EINPROGRESS state)
  • epoll_data encoding is correct for each session: session_index | venue << 8 | protocol << 16
Session Expected epoll_data encoding 0 (FIX BIST) 0 \| BIST << 8 \| FIX << 16 1 (OUCH BIST) 1 \| BIST << 8 \| OUCH << 16 2 (OUCH NASDAQ) 2 \| NASDAQ << 8 \| OUCH << 16

docs.title: 2. TCP Handshake
docs.text:
Verifies that all three TCP connections complete successfully once recv_send() starts processing epoll events.

NetworkIO handles EINPROGRESS on the epoll loop — on EPOLLOUT for a pending socket it completes the handshake and transitions the socket to connected state. The test waits for all three fake servers to receive the accepted client connection before proceeding.

docs.title: 3. Login Sequence
docs.text:
Verifies that NetworkIO sends login request messages to each server immediately after connection, and that sessions transition to logged-in state after receiving login acknowledgements.

  • FIX session (0): SessionState is set manually — FIX login ack is handled by Parser_FIX, not SBTPacketHandler, so the test simulates this by calling setSessionLoggedIn(0, true) directly
  • OUCH BIST (1) and OUCH NASDAQ (2): fake servers send back sbt_login_accepted_bist and sbt_login_accepted_nq — SBTPacketHandler processes these and updates SessionManager

All three sessions reach logged-in state before the traffic phase begins.

docs.title: 4. Outbound Order Sending (Tx Path)
docs.text:
Verifies that NetworkIO correctly transmits outbound packets built by Builder_Dispatch.

Three test orders are pushed to the risk_to_builder queue and dispatched:

Order Venue Protocol fix_new_order BIST FIX ouch_new_order BIST OUCH NQouch_new_order NASDAQ OUCH

The test waits until each fake TCP server receives exactly 2 messages — the login request sent on connection plus the order packet. Confirms the Tx path from builder_to_sender queue through NetworkIO::send() to the socket.

docs.text:
Unit tests for OrderManager — the component responsible for matching incoming market messages (FIX, OUCH, ITCH) to pending orders, updating Order state (status, quantities, timestamps), maintaining the MarketBook, and forwarding updated orders to the risk queue.

Tests are written with Google Test (gtest). The test pushes MessageWithVenue objects directly to the parser_to_store queue and verifies the resulting Order* state on store_to_risk after each store() call.

docs.text:
Component Role OrderManager System under test parser_to_store Input queue — MessageWithVenue pushed by test store_to_risk Output queue — Order* popped for verification MarketBook Updated by ITCH messages, queried to verify best bid/ask HashTables Symbol metadata lookup

Three orders are pre-registered via add_awaitingAck_order() before traffic begins:

Order Venue Protocol Symbol Side Price Qty Token FIX BIST FIX GARAN Buy 15000 500 "F1" / cl_ord_id "O1" OUCH BIST BIST OUCH GARAN Buy 10000 100 "TOKEN000000042" OUCH NASDAQ NASDAQ OUCH AAPL Buy 10000 1000 "CLIENT0000001 "

docs.title: OrderManagerTest.MixedMessageTraffic
docs.text: Processes 20 messages across all protocols and venues, verifying Order state transitions, quantity tracking, and MarketBook updates at each step.

docs.title: Setup — SymbolMeta Initialization
docs.text:
Before order traffic, two directory messages initialize symbol metadata:

  • NASDAQ ITCH StockDirectory — AAPL (stock_locate=1)

Unit tests for Parser_Dispatch — the component responsible for routing inbound RxPackets to the correct protocol parser (FIX, OUCH BIST, OUCH NASDAQ, ITCH BIST, ITCH NASDAQ), reassembling fragmented messages, and pushing parsed MessageWithVenue structs to the downstream queue.

Tests are written with Google Test (gtest). The test feeds raw RxPacket objects directly into the parser queue, bypassing NetworkIO, to test parsing logic in isolation.

docs.title: ParserDispatchTest.MixedProtocolTraffic
docs.text: End-to-end parsing of interleaved multi-protocol traffic across OUCH BIST, ITCH BIST, FIX, and ITCH NASDAQ. Tests correct fragmentation reassembly, protocol routing, field extraction, and output ordering under realistic mixed-protocol conditions.

docs.title: Input Dataset
docs.text:
13 raw RxPackets are injected in the following order — deliberately interleaved to stress protocol boundary handling:

# Packet Protocol Type 1 ouch_bist_RxPacket_partial_1 OUCH BIST Fragment 1/5 2 ouch_bist_RxPacket_partial_2 OUCH BIST Fragment 2/5 3 itch_bist_RxPacket_single_1 ITCH BIST Complete 4 fix_RxPacket_partial_1 FIX Fragment 1/6 5 fix_RxPacket_partial_2 FIX Fragment 2/6 6 ouch_bist_RxPacket_partial_3 OUCH BIST Fragment 3/5 7 ouch_bist_RxPacket_partial_4 OUCH BIST Fragment 4/5 8 fix_RxPacket_partial_3 FIX Fragment 3/6 9 fix_RxPacket_partial_4 FIX Fragment 4/6 10 ouch_bist_RxPacket_partial_5 OUCH BIST Fragment 5/5 11 itch_nasdaq_RxPacket_single_1 ITCH NASDAQ Complete 12 fix_RxPacket_partial_5 FIX Fragment 5/6 13 fix_RxPacket_partial_6 FIX Fragment 6/6

OUCH packets pass through SBTPacketHandler for SoupBinTCP framing before entering the parser queue. FIX and ITCH packets are pushed directly. dispatch() is called 12 times to process all input.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Unit tests for RiskEngine — the component responsible for two distinct paths:

  • Update path (update_risk()) — processes incoming order lifecycle events (new, partial fill, execution, cancel) from store_to_risk, updating AccountRisk, SymbolRisk, and OrderRisk structs with exposure, position, PnL, and margin calculations.
  • Check path (check_risk()) — validates outbound orders from strategy against all configured risk limits before forwarding to the builder, returning structured reject reasons for any violation.

Tests are written with Google Test (gtest). The test is split into two sequential sections within a single test case, sharing the same RiskEngine instance.

Risk struct layout verified per update:

docs.text: End-to-end test of both risk paths across BIST and NASDAQ, covering full order lifecycle and all configured risk limit checks.

docs.title: Part 1 — Update Risk
docs.text:
15 orders processed through update_risk() in sequence. BIST (GARAN) and NASDAQ (AAPL) run in parallel — each venue has independent AccountRisk and SymbolRisk state.

Scaling notes: remaining_qty in OrderRisk is stored in round lots (quantity / round_lot_size). current_leverage uses a 10,000 scale factor. Fee deductions use a 1,000,000 scale factor.

docs.title: Part 2 — Check Risk
docs.text:
Risk state reset to clean baseline before check tests begin. Tick size table initialized (GARAN: tick size 10, range 0–100M). best_bid=10000, best_ask=10000.

15 orders tested against check_risk(). Each order is designed to trigger a specific limit violation. One order passes all checks.

docs.title: Check 1 — Pass
docs.text: Valid order within all limits. risk_to_strategy receives rej_order.order == nullptr — order forwarded to builder, not rejected.

docs.title: Check 2 — MinOrderSizeExceeded
docs.text: Order quantity below the configured minimum order size for the symbol.

docs.title: Check 3 — MaxOrderSizeExceeded
docs.text: Order quantity above the configured maximum order size for the symbol.

docs.title: Check 4 — InvalidLotSize
docs.text: Order quantity is not a multiple of the symbol's round lot size.

docs.title: Check 5 — MaxOrderNotionalLimitExceeded + InvalidPriceRange
docs.text: best_bid set to 180,000 before check. Order price deviates beyond the allowed range from best bid, and the resulting notional exceeds the per-order notional limit. Both flags set simultaneously in the reject bitmask.

docs.title: Check 6 — PriceTickInvalid
docs.text: Order price is not aligned to the tick size (tick size = 10, price not divisible by 10).

docs.title: Check 7 — FatFingerCheckFailed
docs.text: Order price deviates beyond the fat finger threshold from the reference price.

docs.title: Check 8 — MaxPositionLimitExceeded
docs.text: net_position set to 960 before check — the incoming order would push position beyond the configured symbol position limit.

docs.title: Check 9 — MaxNotionalLimitExceeded
docs.text: current_exposure set to 49,900,000 before check — the incoming order's notional would push account exposure beyond the configured notional limit.

docs.title: Check 10 — AccountBalanceInsufficient + FreeMarginInsufficient + MaxLeverageExceeded
docs.text: balance set to 10,000 before check. Three limits triggered simultaneously — insufficient balance, free margin below required level, and resulting leverage above maximum. All three flags set in reject bitmask.

docs.title: Check 11 — MaxOpenOrdersReachedAccount
docs.text: open_orders_count set to 5 at account level — at the configured maximum. New order rejected.

docs.title: Check 12 — MaxOpenOrdersReachedSymbol
docs.text: open_orders_count set to 3 at symbol level — at the configured maximum for this symbol.

docs.title: Check 13 — SelfTradeDetected
docs.text: An OrderRisk entry is manually inserted at the same price, side, symbol, and venue as the incoming order before the check. Self-trade detection identifies the matching resting order.

docs.title: Check 14 — UnrealizedLossLimitExceeded
docs.text: Unrealized PnL on the position (best_bid below avg entry) has breached the configured unrealized loss limit.

docs.title: Check 15 — RealizedLossLimitExceeded
docs.text: avg_entry_price set to 30,000 before check. Closing at current price would realize a loss beyond the configured daily realized loss limit.

docs.title: Check 16 — MaxOrderRateLimitExceededSymbol + MaxOrderRateLimitExceededAccount
docs.text: Checks whether the number of orders sent within a predefined time window exceeds the allowed limit. Implemented using rate-limit token buckets.
